newsitem.title: USA: Moynihan stadiums expert taking key Treasury post.
newsitem.headline: Moynihan stadiums expert taking key Treasury post.

text.p: John Talisman, a top advisor to U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan on the volatile stadium bonds issue, is expected shortly to be named Tax Legislative Counsel for U.S. Treasury Department, where among his duties he will take on the controversial "yield burning" issue, reliable sources said Friday.

A Treasury spokesman said he could not confirm that Talisman is moving to Treasury. Talisman, who is chief tax counsel on the minority staff of the Senate Finance Committee, also refused to comment when contacted by Reuters.
Moynihan, D-N.Y., is ranking Democrat on Finance.
On Capitol Hill, Talisman is a top advisor to Moynihan on the senator's controversial bill to bar the use of tax-exempt bonds to finance construction of professional sports stadiums.
At Treasury, Talisman would help oversee policy by the department on "yield burning" and other issues, sources said.
Yield burning refers to explosive allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuer for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing deals.
IRS last year stunned localities with a "closing agreement" plan that says issuers can head off having interest on their bonds declared taxable by making certain payments to Treasury.
Muni bond industry groups are set to meet at 1100 EST Jan 27 with Donald Lubick, Treasury's assistant secretary for tax policy on the issue.
Talisman would take over the tax counsel post at Treasury from Michael Thomson. Sources did not know where Thomson is going.
